report.tagline: A US company that sells connected exercise bikes, treadmills and rowers plus a monthly membership for live and on-demand classes.
report.simpleSummary: Peloton sells an exercise bike or treadmill with a big screen. You pay a monthly membership to stream live and recorded classes led by energetic instructors, with a leaderboard so you can race other riders. It was a pandemic star, with sales doubling when gyms closed, then crashed when gyms reopened. Today it is smaller, sells fewer machines, but makes a small profit because most of its money comes from memberships.

overview.whatItDoes: Peloton makes connected fitness hardware: Bike, Bike+, Tread, Row and the Cross Training series. Owners pay for the All-Access Membership to take classes in cycling, running, strength, yoga and more. People without hardware can use the Peloton App on phones, TVs or gym equipment. It also sells used and refurbished machines and commercial equipment for hotels and gyms.
howItWorks: A customer buys or rents a Peloton machine online or in a showroom, often with monthly financing.
The machine connects to the internet and streams live and on-demand classes on its screen.
The All-Access Membership unlocks classes, metrics and the leaderboard for everyone in the household.
Instructors become personalities; riders follow favourites and join live classes.
Peloton IQ and other software features suggest workouts and track progress.
App-only members pay less and use classes with any equipment.
overview.valueProposition: A boutique fitness class experience at home, any time, with motivating instructors and a sense of community, so you actually keep working out.

businessModel.summary: Peloton sells hardware, often at low margin, to lock people into a high-margin monthly membership. Most of its revenue and almost all its gross profit now come from subscriptions.

revenueStreams.detail: All-Access Membership for hardware owners and Peloton App tiers; the majority of revenue.
Sales and rentals of Bike, Tread, Row and accessories.
Machines for hotels, gyms and used equipment sales.

businessModel.pricing: All-Access Membership is about $44 to $50 a month in the US after the October 2025 price rise; app tiers are cheaper. Bikes start at roughly $1,500, with rentals and refurbished options. Check the site for current prices.
businessModel.unitEconomics: A typical member pays about $45 a month, or about $540 a year. Content and music cost the same whether Peloton has 2 or 3 million members, so subscriptions have high gross margins. With monthly churn of about 2%, an average member stays about four years, worth roughly $2,000 in membership revenue. That is the LTV (lifetime value). Hardware is sold near cost, so the real question is whether the marketing and hardware discount to win a member costs less than that LTV.

growth.moat: Peloton's moat is its brand, its instructors and its 2.5 million paying members who already own the hardware. Switching means buying a new machine. But the classes are copyable, and cheaper bikes with app-based classes are common.

pmLessons: A temporary boom is not a new normal. Peloton built factories for pandemic demand that never came back.
Hardware can be a hook for a subscription. The membership is the real business.
Price rises can raise revenue but also churn. Measure both.
Community and personalities are a product. Instructors are a big reason people stay.

interviewQuestions.question: Peloton's churn rose from 1.8% to 2.2% after a price increase. What would you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment who churned, compare to usage, test tiers or discounts, and calculate whether extra revenue outweighs lost LTV.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Peloton keep making hardware or become a pure software company?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare churn of hardware vs app members, margins, brand, and competition; propose a mixed strategy.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to get new Bike owners to their 10th workout.
interviewQuestions.hint: Map the first 30 days, find drop-offs, propose onboarding programmes and nudges, track activation.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow the Peloton App without hardware?
interviewQuestions.hint: Target gym users and cheap-bike owners, partner with gyms, differentiate from Apple Fitness+.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Peloton's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Engaged members (workouts per month), and how it drives churn and revenue.
